description: Generate a code coverage report for a .NET project or solution via `dotnet test --collect:"XPlat Code Coverage"` (the Coverlet collector) — or, for test projects on Microsoft.Testing.Platform, the platform's `--coverage` extension — scoped to the test selector given (same selector syntax as the `iru-dotnet-test` skill), then read the generated `coverage.cobertura.xml` to report the exact line-coverage percentage for the specific class(es) touched — using that same file's per-line `hits` data to show which lines/branches are still uncovered. Uses the repository's `tests/coverlet.runsettings` (Cobertura + OpenCover formats, attribute exclusions) when present. Windows-desktop aware — on a non-Windows host it passes `-p:EnableWindowsTargeting=true` and measures only test projects that can run there, always excludes `[TestCategory("UI")]` UI-automation tests (they never count toward coverage), and for a Windows desktop app (WPF/WinUI 3/Windows Forms) measures the UI-free Core project while reporting the app/UI assemblies as "not measured" rather than 0%. Invoke as `/iru-dotnet-coverage <selector> [TargetClass1,TargetClass2,...]`, or `/iru-dotnet-coverage` with no argument to run the full suite and report whole-solution coverage; optional `key: value` lines — `project: <test-project>`, `bar: <percent>`. Use whenever the user wants to check, or verify a coverage bar (e.g. "at least 80% line coverage") for a class or set of classes, instead of eyeballing `dotnet test` output.
